system:
You are coding NSW motor accident decisions for a research dataset. Read the decision text supplied and assign each ordinal score from the text alone.

Score each dimension INDEPENDENTLY. A decision describing a severe case will score high on some dimensions and not others: severe physical injury does not by itself imply a contested proceeding, a disputed liability, or a prominent psychological component. Judge each scale against its own definition and resist letting an overall impression of severity carry across the scales.

If the text does not support a judgement on a dimension, give the lowest score rather than guessing upward, and say so in `uncertain`.

DECISION TEXT:
--- Catchwords ---
MOTOR ACCIDENTS -

Motor Accident Injuries Act 2017 ; settlement approval under section 6.23(2)(b) ; accident as driver; claimant sustained right shoulder injuries and psychological condition; not entitled to non-economic loss; long period off work; permanently restricted from pre-injury duties; medical evidence supports deterioration and early retirement; coexisting morbidities from non-accident related conditions; insurer accepted claimant's offer; claimant commercially minded and expressed himself as having agency to decide on accepting settlement; proposed settlement fair, just and reasonable; Held – proposed settlement approved.

--- Key Paragraphs ---
[para 17] Sets out s 6.23 MAI Act framework governing settlement approvals.
17. Section 6.23 of the MAI Act imposes restrictions on the settlement of a claim for damages. That provision is, relevantly, in the following terms: "6.23 Restrictions on settlement of claim for damages

(1) (Repealed)

(2) A claim for damages cannot be settled unless—

(a) ...

(b) the proposed settlement is approved by the Commission.

(3) The Commission is not to approve the settlement of a claim unless satisfied that the settlement complies with any applicable requirements of or made under this Act or the Motor Accident Guidelines."

[para 18] Recites cl 7.37 Guidelines approval criteria including fairness and understanding.
18. Clause 7.37 of the Motor Accident Guidelines states as follows: "7.37 Under section 6.23(3) of the Act, before the Personal Injury Commission may approve the settlement of a claim for damages, it must be satisfied that:

(a) (Omitted)

(b) the proposed settlement is just, fair and reasonable and within the range of likely potential damages assessments for the claim were the matter to be assessed by the Commission, taking into account the nature and extent of the claim and the injuries, disabilities, impairments and losses sustained by the claimant, and taking into account any proposed reductions or deductions in the proposed settlement

(c) the claimant understands that they are entitled to be represented in respect of the claim by an Australian legal practitioner

(d) the claimant understands the nature and effect of the proposed settlement and is willing to accept the proposed settlement."

[para 31] Finds accident primary cause of shoulder condition despite premorbid issues.
31. The specialist noted the right shoulder had a full range of motion in the right shoulder. He also opined that the claimant would return to full fitness after the accident. The specialist accepted that despite the claimant having premorbid illnesses and orthopaedic problems the accident was the primary cause of his right shoulder condition. EVIDENCE OF ECONOMIC LOSS

[para 42] Explains past economic loss methodology including buffer and components.
42. The settlement of $109,000 is based on a past buffer of $85,000 noting any loss is likely to be ongoing and the claimant's earnings were difficult to assess with precision due to fluctuations based on the availability of work.

[para 47] Details vicissitudes discount and cites Commonwealth v Elliott and Tomes v Adams.
47. The insurer applied the conventional 15% discount for vicissitudes despite the potential to argue that a higher discount may be warranted due to the claimant's non accident-related conditions: see Commonwealth of Australia v Elliott

[2004] NSWCA 360 per Giles JA (with whom Hodgson and Tobias JJA agreed) at [81]; Tomes v Adams

[2003] NSWCA 269.

[para 50] Calculates initial future loss period with multiplier and discount.
50. The amount allowed for future economic loss is calculated on a loss of $350 net per week for two years (multiplier 99.4) less 15% for vicissitudes produces $29,571.50.

[para 55] Core conclusion that settlement is within range and just for approval.
55. I accepted that the final settlement figure was within the range of possible settlement. It was just, because the claimant had been given the opportunity to seek legal advice, he is a commercially minded man and he has agency to choose not to have legal representation, consider the insurer's offer and judge if it will adequately compensate him.

[para 58] Formal approval order under s 6.23(2)(b) MAI Act.
58. The proposed settlement of $465,000 all-inclusive is approved under s 6.23(2)(b) of the MAI Act.

Assign each score:
  Injury Burden Intensity (0-4): overall physical burden of the injuries: 0 minimal, 4 catastrophic/multiple major injuries
  Treatment Burden (0-3): extent of treatment, surgery and ongoing care: 0 none or minimal, 3 extensive surgery and long-term care
  Work Impact Severity (0-3): loss of working capacity: 0 none, 3 total incapacity
  Legal Procedural Complexity (0-3): procedural complexity of the proceeding: 0 straightforward, 3 heavily contested
  Psychological Injury Emphasis (0-2): weight the decision gives to psychological injury: 0 none, 2 central
  Liability Clarity (0-2): how clear fault is: 0 seriously disputed, 2 clear or admitted
  Causation Complexity (0-2): difficulty attributing the condition to the accident: 0 straightforward, 2 heavily contested
  Pre-existing Condition Salience (0-2): how prominent a prior condition is in the decision: 0 absent, 2 central
